findings.title: Wrong default for cook_method flips existing posts to raw_html
findings.body: The migration adds cook_method with default 1, null false. Post.cook_methods is Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html) so regular is 0 and raw_html is 1. Every existing row therefore defaults to raw_html, and Post#cook returns raw without cooking. After migrating, all historic cooked HTML is bypassed and raw markdown is rendered, breaking display and bypassing sanitization.

findings.title: Stored XSS via unsanitized imported HTML rendered raw
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import stores feed/readability HTML with cook_method raw_html, Post#cook returns raw verbatim, and app/views/embed/best.html.erb renders it with raw post.cooked. There is no sanitization of tags, attributes, script, or of the interpolated url in the imported_from footer. A malicious feed or embedded page can store arbitrary JS that executes in the embed iframe and, via postMessage/parent context, attacks the host site.

findings.title: Reflected XSS via unescaped request.referer in postMessage
findings.body: The layout interpolates <%= request.referer %> directly inside a single-quoted JS string for postMessage targetOrigin. Referer is attacker-controlled by the embedding site and is not JS-escaped. A referer containing a quote and script breaks out of the string and executes in the embed origin. It is also the wrong value: targetOrigin must be an origin, not a full URL.

findings.title: Reversed postMessage origin check allows prefix spoof
findings.body: The handler checks discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1, i.e. whether the configured URL contains the event origin. An attacker origin that is a prefix of discourseUrl passes, e.g. e.origin http://forum.example accepted when discourseUrl is http://forum.example.com/. The check must compare origins for equality, not test containment in the wrong direction.

findings.title: PollFeed crashes on nil content and unhandled fetch errors
findings.body: SimpleRSS items may have nil content/link. The code calls i.content.scrub and CGI.unescapeHTML on it unconditionally, raising NoMethodError and aborting the hourly job. open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) and SimpleRSS.parse can also raise on network, timeout, or malformed feed with no rescue, so one bad poll kills the whole import.

findings.title: Unbounded raw URL used as Redis throttle key
findings.body: retrieved_recently? builds retrieved:#{@embed_url} directly from user-supplied embed_url with no hashing, length limit, or namespacing. An attacker can create unlimited distinct keys and very long keys in Redis, causing memory growth and keyspace pollution. The URL should be hashed, e.g. SHA1, before use as a key.

findings.title: Import mutates caller string with << causing double footer
findings.body: contents << footer mutates the caller's string in place instead of duplicating it. Reusing the same string for a second import appends the Imported from footer twice, changing content_sha1 and stored raw on every call and breaking idempotent update detection.

findings.title: absolutize_urls raises InvalidURIError on bad URL
findings.body: absolutize_urls calls URI(url) with no rescue. import only guards with url =~ /^https?\:\/\//, which still allows strings that URI rejects. An exception escapes PostCreator/TopicRetriever/PollFeed paths and turns a single bad feed item or embed_url into a 500 or failed job instead of skipping it.

findings.title: Embed controller spec expects TopicRetriever but code enqueues job
findings.body: The controller enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) on a miss, but the spec stubs TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed to nil and expects TopicRetriever.new/retrieve. The spec does not exercise the actual code path and will fail or pass for the wrong reason, leaving the loading branch untested.
